## Science Question

How does water quality (temperature and chlorophyll-a) vary across time and among drinking water reservoirs in the Roanoke region?

## Science Question

-   Chlorophyll-a is a pigment in plants, algae, and cyanobacteria that used in photosynthesis. It is a metric of how much algae is present in the lake or reservoir.

-   Too much cause aesthetic problems such as green scums and bad odors, and can result in decreased levels of dissolved oxygen. (U.S. EPA)

-   Some algae and cyanobacteria also produce toxins that can be of public health concern when they are found in high concentrations. (U.S. EPA)

[<https://www.epa.gov/national-aquatic-resource-surveys/indicators-chlorophyll>]{.aside}

## Data

## Data

A CTD (Conductivity, Temperature, and Depth) sensor is lowered in the water column and uses sensors to measure different water quality variables throughout the water column.

## Reservoirs

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
#| message: false

library(sf)
library(leaflet)
sites <- suppressMessages(sf::st_read("sites.json"))
```

```{r}
#| fig.height: 5
#| fig.width: 10
#| fig-alt: Interactive map of reservoirs used in the module
#| message: false

leaflet() %>%
  setView(lat = 37.2, lng = -80.35, zoom= 10) %>%
  addTiles(group="OSM") %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery, group="Imagery") %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldTopoMap, group="Topo Map") %>%
  addLayersControl(baseGroups=c('Imagery','OSM', 'Topo Map')) |> 
  addMarkers(data  = sites, popup=~as.character(site_id), group = ~as.character(Partner), clusterOptions = markerClusterOptions())
```
